story: The Space Quest II Master Disk Blunder
text: I can give you an example of someone claiming there were holes in the disk, Jon Burton, but they're a goddamn liar : [VIDEO] I have the original release of Leander. There are no holes in the disks. The code on the disk doesn't write anything besides hiscores. There is a protection routine exactly where he says there is, however what it does is check for a long track . It waits for the index pin, reads lots of data from the track, then looks to find two sync marks in the data it read, and they're at least a certain distance away from each other. No lasers, no holes, no writing. Standard long track protection. Here's the whole routine: [LINK] Here's a page that more accurately describes floppy disk protection methods (and also explains what a long track is): [LINK]
